title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Java switches, Javadoc, and a prompt that keeps its word
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.16 fixes a regression of 1.42.15 in Java switches, stops the rating prompt from re-arming on every window, renders Javadoc HTML in hovers instead of showing the tags, and corrects the call hierarchy, Expand Selection, the chat participant and the Find Usages panel where they told you something false.

highlights.title: Lambda parameters on a case line, back
highlights.description: The 1.42.15 rule for switch arms stopped at -> but not at :, so `case RED: items.forEach(i -> log(i))` lost the binding of i and Rename treated it as a workspace symbol. Fixed, with the arrow form still handled.

highlights.title: Javadoc rendered, not shown
highlights.description:
Since 1.42.14 the generic escape showed

, and

    literally on Java methods. The common tags and {@code} / {@link} become Markdown, generics still survive, and the rating prompt persists its count before showing so it stops re-arming on every window.

highlights.title: Call hierarchy and Expand Selection told the truth
highlights.description: A call in a property initializer was attributed to the function above it and an overload's declaration was listed as a caller; Expand Selection swallowed the next declaration's KDoc and @Composable. Both stop at the right line now, and the chat participant reads "usages of the Foo class".

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Anchors the qualified-R rule at the start of the qualifier: a module named com.example.android keeps its R, and Google gms/firebase R classes are excluded like AndroidX.
Says when the Find Usages panel is stale after an edit, and highlights $name in string templates like Find Usages counts it.
